sources.entry: NAPI - Defines the polling, software coalescing, busy polling and IRQ suspension knobs that trade interrupts against latency.

summary.title: NAPI
summary.one_liner: NAPI is the Linux networking stack's hybrid interrupt/polling event mechanism, and this kernel doc explains its driver API, scheduling rules, and the software coalescing, busy polling, and IRQ suspension knobs that trade interrupts against latency.
keywords: how does linux network driver interrupt polling work
takeaways: NAPI combines device interrupts with polling: an interrupt schedules a NAPI instance whose poll method processes Rx and Tx work within a budget.
Drivers must call napi_complete_done() only when work is finished, and must follow the budget rules (return budget or budget - 1) to avoid lost wakeups.
Software coalescing is controlled by gro_flush_timeout and napi_defer_hard_irqs; busy polling via SO_BUSY_POLL or epoll trades CPU for lower latency.
IRQ suspension (irq-suspend-timeout with SO_PREFER_BUSY_POLL) keeps device IRQs masked while epoll retrieves events, and works best combined with gro_flush_timeout and napi_defer_hard_irqs.
summary.summary: The page is the Linux kernel documentation for NAPI, the event handling mechanism of the networking stack. It describes the driver API (struct napi_struct and the poll method), the control API (netif_napi_add, napi_enable/disable), and the datapath rules for scheduling, IRQ masking, budgets, and completion. It then covers user-facing configuration: queue-to-NAPI mapping, persistent NAPI config, netlink-based tuning, software IRQ coalescing, busy polling (sysctl, socket option, and epoll ioctl), IRQ suspension, and threaded NAPI and threaded busy polling. Examples use the tools/net/ynl cli.py script and ynl netlink commands.
